full_judgment:
M Enayetur Rahim J: This Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 9-8-1993 passed by the Sessions Judge, Dhaka, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1313 of 1993 and as the senior Special Judge in the Special Case No. 946 of 1993 should not be set- aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. (As written in the Rule issuing order.) 

 2. The present accused-petitioner on 17-2- 1993 at about 1.00 PM was apprehended with a pistol and 6 cartridges from the crossing point of Road No. 14, and Shere Bangla Road of Dhanmondi area by the police personnel who were on petrol duty in that area; with regard to recovery of such pistol and cartridges Dhanmondi Police Station Case No. 21 (2)93 under section 19A and (f) of the Arms Act, 1878 was started against the accused-petitioner. 

 3. The police after investigation into the case submitted charge-sheet against the petitioner on 18-6-1993 under section 19A and (f) of the Arms Act. 

 4. Thereafter the accused-petitioner moved an application before the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka, to transfer the case to the Juvenile Court stating that the age of the accused-petitioner was below 16 years at the time of the alleged occurrence. The said application was registered as criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 313 of 1992. When the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1313 of 1993 was pending before the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka the case record was sent to the senior Special Tribunal, Dhaka, and the case was registered as Special Case No. 946 of 1993 and the learned Judge of the Tribunal by its order dated 9- 8-1993 took cognizance into the Case against the accused-petitioner under section 19(A) and (f) of the Arms Act. 

 5. The learned Sessions Judge after hearing the respective parties by the impugned judgment and order dated 9-8-1993 rejected the Criminal Miscellaneous Case. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and order refusing to transfer the case to the Juvenile Court, the accused-petitioner by filing an application under section 439(1) read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has obtained the present Rule. 

 9. In the instant case, the Rule was issued on 22-8-1993 and admittedly on that date charge was not framed against the accused-petitioner by any Court particularly the Special Tribunal constituted under the Special Powers Act, 1974 where the offence in question is to be tried. After issuance of the Rule by this time more than 18 years have already been elapsed and having regard to the fact that in the meantime the accused-petitioner has become a major. 

 10. Though High Court Division in the cases of Md Shamim vs State, reported in 19 BLD 542 and Monir Hossain vs State, reported in 53 DLR 411 held that the trial by the Special Tribunal in respect of an accused who was under 16 years at the time of commissioning offence is without jurisdiction; but our Appellate Division in the cases of Abdul Monem Chowdhury @ Monem vs State, reported in 47 DLR (AD) 96 and Mona alias Zillur Rahman vs State reported in 23 BLD (AD) 187 has not approved the above view of the High Court Division. 

 11. In the case of Abdul Monem Chowdhury alias Monem vs State Appellate Division held that; 

 12. In the Case of Mona alias Zillur Rahman vs The State, the Appellate Division also held that; 

 13. On perusal of the above reported Case it appears to us that our Appellate Division has taken the view that the reckoning 'date for the determination of the age of the juvenile is the date of framing of charge and not the date of commission of the alleged offence. 

 15. Mr Khan also tried to impress us that since those decisions were passed by the Appellate Division in leave Petitions and in a summary manner, that cannot be treated or considered as the declared law as contemplated in Article 111 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. We are also unable to accept the said submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. Supreme Court of India in the case of Protap Singh vs State of Jharkhand, reported in (2005), 3 SCC 551 has decided that the determination of the age of the juvenile is the date of the offence and not the date when he is produced before the authority or in the Court. Same view has been taken in the Case of the Umesh Singh vs State of Bihar, reported in (2000) 6 Supreme Court Cases, 89. 

 16. Since our Appellate Division has decided the issue involved in the instant case, we are binding by the decision and observation of our Appellate Division. The decision of Indian Supreme Court is not binding upon us. 

 17. Further it appears to us the accused-petitioner before raising the question of jurisdiction , before the trial Court that is the Special Tribunal had filed Miscellaneous Case before the Sessions Judge to transfer case in Juvenile Court. It is by now settled proposition of law that the trial Court is the competent Court to determine its jurisdiction to try a particular case. In the instant case, before transmitting the Case record to the trial Court, that is the Special Tribunal, the accused- petitioner without waiting to raise any objection as to its jurisdiction before it hurriedly moved an application before the learned Sessions Judge making prayer to transfer the case to the Juvenile Court. Thus, we are of the view that the said application was absolutely misconceived and not tenable in law. 

 18. In the instant case charge has not been framed as yet against the petitioner and, as such, we are of the view that the accused-petitioner has no leg to stand. The issue raised by the accused- petitioner has no force of law. Accordingly, we find no merit in this Rule. 

 20.	The impugned judgment and order dated 9-8-1993 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 946 of 1993 is hereby affirmed. 

 22. The Special Tribunal is directed to proceed with the case in accordance with law keeping in the mind that at the time of occurrence the age of accused-petitioner was below 16 years. The trial Court is directed to issue notice upon the accused-petitioner to appear before it; failing which the Tribunal should proceed with the case in accordance with law. If the accused-petitioner is surrendered as per the direction of the Tribunal, the Tribunal shall consider the prayer for bail in accordance with law keeping the fact in mind that he was granted bail by the High Court Division and for last 18 years he has been enjoying the privilege of bail.
